flow.caption_zh: 早期九份電影院“昇平戲院”的廣告看板。

zh: 鹿港深巷？ 台南古街？
en: The mountain path winds, silver grass swaying
Jiufen's mountain town, fine rain falling
The northeast coast
Outlines uneven
Lost in haze amid cloud, mist, and vapor
The steps of Shuqi Road
Step after step
Looking at it, there seems no end
The street's face winding and narrow
As if walking through a corridor of history
A deep lane in Lukang? An old street in Tainan?
This moment
If a strain of Nanguan music were to strike up
Thread by thread, urgent and close
Pulling back a stretch of hardship-worn years

zh: 仿若一脈細流沿岸風景
“ 我達達的馬蹄聲是個錯誤
偏遠、貧寂、繁華、沒落、復起
怎樣的歷史悲情，人事滄桑
怎樣的戀戀風塵，綿綿舊情
en: Treading the brick and flagstone road
Teahouses and shops stand packed row upon row
As if a thin stream of scenery along the shore
Streetlamps sparse, umbrella shadows flickering
Footsteps keep company with the sound of rain
Rising and falling, dripping and ticking
"My clip-clopping hoofbeats are a mistake
I am not one returning, but a passer-by”
Remote, poor and quiet, prosperous, declined, risen again
This small mountain town
After all, still bearing the weight of
What historical sorrow, what vicissitudes of human affairs
What lingering worldly love, what unbroken old affection
Since I must look back
Keeping company with homesickness forever
Once more must hope
Racing the tides of time for speed
Like being drunk on old wine
Misty fog, flower shadows
Leaving one hesitant, unable to grasp it
Bidding farewell to the mountain town in the rain
The dried-up Keelung River, accompanied by
The fast lane
Rain outside the window, dripping drop by drop
Gazing far into the dusk
Taipei, drawing nearer step by step
Cannot help but let questions rise, one after another
When will I be the one who returns
Not just a passer-by?

points.zh: 九份位於新北市瑞芳區，臨近金瓜石和雞籠山，是昔日的採金礦中心。環山面海，擁有多變的山海美景，是座小小的山城，保有純樸的舊日生活風貌。根據《台北縣誌》的文獻記載，在清朝初期，這貧寂村落只住了九户人家，因此每當外出到市集購物或是貨船來到，都是每樣要九份，遂稱此村落為九份，地名一直沿用至今。九份和金瓜石的金礦開採至少有一百年的歷史。1894年在九份一帶發現金礦礦脈，淘金和採金的人潮大批湧入，展開了九份繁華的鎏金歲月，在黄金開採最盛時期，九份曾經嬴得「小香港」或「小上海」的稱呼，當地人民的消費能力甚至凌駕台北之上，據說當時全台灣最好的酒家和餐館都集中在九份，台灣第一家電影院「昇平戲院」也在九份建立，其繁華景象可見一斑。1956年以後，九份一帶的金礦已大至採盡，產業没落之後，九份的風光便走向歷史。人口流散，殘街空户，衰敗蕭條景象漫延叢生。直到1990年代後，侯孝賢導演，吳念真編劇，所拍攝的電影「悲情城市」和「戀戀風塵」在九份取景，九份獨特的舊式街道建築，坡地石階，蒼桑風情，以及山海景色，透過電影而吸引國内外的注目，也為九份重新帶來生機和活力。這是一個沒落城市因電影的渲染而浴火重生的典型例子。九份的懷舊之美，文化傳承以及新潮人文風華的加注，所營造的藝術山城氛圍，在台灣觀光休閒產業上，開始散發著閃耀的光芒。
points.en: Jiufen is located in Ruifang District, New Taipei City, near Jinguashi and Jilong Mountain, and was once a center of gold mining. Surrounded by mountains and facing the sea, it possesses ever-changing mountain and ocean scenery, and is a small mountain town that retains the simple, rustic character of earlier times. According to records in the "Taipei County Gazetteer," in the early Qing dynasty this poor, remote village had only nine households, so whenever people went out to the market to shop or when cargo ships arrived, each of the nine households would need a share -- hence the village came to be called "Jiufen" (literally "nine shares"), a name still in use today. Gold mining in Jiufen and Jinguashi has a history of at least a hundred years. In 1894, a gold vein was discovered in the Jiufen area, and large crowds of gold prospectors and miners poured in, beginning Jiufen's golden age of prosperity. At the height of gold mining, Jiufen once earned the nickname "Little Hong Kong" or "Little Shanghai," and local residents' spending power reportedly even exceeded that of Taipei. It is said that the finest establishments and restaurants in all of Taiwan were concentrated in Jiufen at the time, and Taiwan's first movie theater, Shengping Theater, was also built there -- a glimpse of its former prosperity. After 1956, the gold deposits in the Jiufen area were largely exhausted, and following the decline of the mining industry, Jiufen's glory days became history. The population scattered, streets fell into disrepair, and empty houses spread as decline and desolation set in. It was not until the 1990s, when director Hou Hsiao-hsien and screenwriter Wu Nien-jen filmed "A City of Sadness" and "Dust in the Wind" on location in Jiufen, that Jiufen's distinctive old-style street architecture, hillside stone steps, weathered atmosphere, and mountain-and-sea scenery attracted attention from home and abroad through these films, bringing renewed vitality and energy back to Jiufen. This is a classic example of a declining town being reborn through the influence of film. Jiufen's nostalgic beauty, its cultural heritage, and the added flourish of new-wave humanistic style have created an artistic mountain-town atmosphere that has begun to shine brightly within Taiwan's tourism and leisure industry.

points.zh: 一般所謂九份老街是由基山街，輕便街和豎﨑路三條老街縱横組成。豎﨑路是九份最早的街道，依山勢建築，全線由石頭砌成，約有三，四百石階石梯，階梯兩旁設滿茶樓，也可見「悲情城市」的招牌。台灣第一家電影院「昇平戲院」，座落於豎崎路和基山街交會處。拾階而上，至頂端可一覽九份純樸的山城景象，以及東北角海岸的廣茫視野。
points.en: What is generally referred to as the Jiufen Old Street is formed by three streets running crosswise: Jishan Street, Qingbian Street, and Shuqi Road. Shuqi Road is Jiufen's earliest street, built following the contours of the mountain and paved entirely in stone, with roughly three to four hundred stone steps. Teahouses line both sides of the steps, and signs for the film "A City of Sadness" can also be seen there. Taiwan's first movie theater, Shengping Theater, is located at the intersection of Shuqi Road and Jishan Street. Climbing the steps to the top offers a view of Jiufen's simple, rustic mountain-town scenery, as well as a sweeping view of the northeast coast.

points.zh:
鄭愁予的詩：「錯誤」
「我打江南走過，那等在季節裡的容顏，如蓮花般開落。東風不來，三月的柳絮不飛，你的心如小小的寂寞的城，恰若青石的街道向晚，跫音不響。三月的春帷不揭，你底心是小小的窗扉緊掩。我達達的馬蹄聲，是個錯誤，我不是歸人，是個過客。」
points.en:
Zheng Chouyu's poem, "A Mistake":
"I passed through Jiangnan, where a face waited within the season, opening and falling like a lotus flower. The east wind does not come, the March willow catkins do not fly; your heart is like a small, lonely city, just as the bluestone streets fall silent at dusk, no echo of footsteps. The spring curtain of March is not lifted; your heart is a small window shut tight. My clattering hoofbeats are a mistake — I am not one who returns home, but only a passer-by."
